title: Michal
lead: Saul's younger daughter and David's first wife, the only woman in the Hebrew Bible's stories said to love a man. She saved David from her father, was given to another husband, was taken back by David, and despised him when he danced before the ark.

sections.b: Michal loves David, and Saul uses her as bait, asking a bride-price of a hundred Philistine foreskins (1 Samuel 18:20–27). She lets David down through a window and fools her father's men with a household god in the bed (1 Samuel 19:11–17). While David is a fugitive, Saul gives her to Palti son of Laish (1 Samuel 25:44). David demands her back as the price of a deal with Abner, and her second husband follows her weeping (2 Samuel 3:13–16). When David dances before the ark, she despises him, and the story ends with the note that she had no child to the day of her death (2 Samuel 6:16–23).
